messages.text: Warwickshire close in on County Championship title after skittling Leicestershire

metadata.summary: Warwickshire took a big step towards clinching the Rothesay County Championship title after skittling relegation-threatened Leicestershire for 125 at Edgbaston.
metadata.content: County Championship: Warwickshire close in on title after skittling relegation-threatened Leicestershire | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content County Championship: Warwickshire close in on title after skittling relegation-threatened Leicestershire Thursday's County Championship sees Warwickshire move closer to title after bowling out relegation-threatened Leicestershire for 125 at Edgbaston; Warwickshire win would guarantee a first title since the Covid-shortened 2021 campaign, with second-placed Somerset struggling against Surrey Thursday 24 September 2026 20:02, UK Image: Ethan Bamber stars as Warwickshire bowl out Leicestershire for 125 to move closer to County Championship title Warwickshire took a big step towards clinching the Rothesay County Championship title after skittling relegation-threatened Leicestershire for 125 at Edgbaston. Ahead of the first day's play, Leicestershire announced plans to appeal their 27-point deduction for a substandard pitch at Grace Road in last month's win over Glamorgan - a decision that means their Division One fate could remain up in the air until the final round of fixtures this week. Only two of their batters passed 12 in Birmingham, with in-form Ethan Bamber taking 4-42 and former England seamer Chris Woakes claiming 3-20 for the Bears, who closed on 130-4 to lead by five. messages.text: Premier League in joint call for FIFA reform amid Infantino crisis

metadata.summary: The Premier League and three of its top European counterparts will on Friday issue a joint call for urgent governance reform at FIFA amid the crisis engulfing its president, Gianni Infantino.
metadata.content: Gianni Infantino: Premier League and three other top European leagues to demand FIFA reform | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Gianni Infantino: Premier League and three other top European leagues to demand FIFA reform English football's top flight and its counterparts in Germany, Italy and Spain will demand urgent reform of the game's global governance in a joint statement on Friday, Sky News understands; the joint call comes amid the crisis engulfing its FIFA president Gianni Infantino By Sky News' Mark Kleinman & Rob Harris Thursday 24 September 2026 18:53, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol explains why the Premier League have joined three of its other top European counterparts in demanding a FIFA reform against Gianni Infantino The Premier League and three of its top European counterparts will on Friday issue a joint call for urgent governance reform at FIFA amid the crisis engulfing its president, Gianni Infantino. Sky News can reveal that English football's top flight and the top domestic leagues in Germany, Italy and Spain will publish a collective statement demanding greater consultation on key issues such as the global football calendar. The statement was still in the process of being formally agreed between the quartet of domestic leagues on Thursday afternoon and it was unclear whether it would specifically call for Infantino to stand down. metadata.summary: Anthony Joshua will be in "a world of trouble" against Tyson Fury if he brings the same level of performance as he did in his previous fight, according to Johnny Nelson.

On Thursday, the long-awaited all-British heavyweight clash was finally confirmed for December 11 at Cardiff's Principality Stadium. Joshua comes into the fight on the back of a major scare during his July victory over Kristian Prenga, with the 36-year-old knocked down twice in the opening round before stopping his unheralded opponent in the second. metadata.summary: Frank Warren has revealed that Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will each earn more than any British fighter has previously been paid for a single bout when they finally meet on December 11.
metadata.content: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Both fighters to earn British record paydays for Cardiff clash, says promoter Frank Warren | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Update Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Both fighters to earn British record paydays for Cardiff clash, says promoter Frank Warren Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury have finally agreed to fight in Cardiff on December 11 after a lengthy delay over the venue for their historic all-British heavyweight clash; Fury's promoter Frank Warren shared new details of the negotiations with Sky Sports News Thursday 24 September 2026 18:43, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Andy Scott and John Dennen react to the news that Tyson Fury will fight Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on 11 December Frank Warren has revealed that Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will each earn more than any British fighter has previously been paid for a single bout when they finally meet on December 11. The long-awaited all-British heavyweight showdown was finally confirmed on Thursday as the date and venue - Cardiff's Principality Stadium - were announced by the fight's promoters. It was also reported by Ring Magazine that the WBA world title will be on the line, giving both Fury and Joshua the opportunity to become three-time world champions. Finally! metadata.summary: Matt Fitzpatrick sits two shots off the early lead at the FedEx Open de France, as defending champion Michael Kim topped the leaderboard after a ‘dream start’ at Le Golf National.
metadata.content: Open de France: Michael Kim leads after 'dream start' as Matt Fitzpatrick impresses on low-scoring day at Le Golf National | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Open de France: Michael Kim leads after 'dream start' as Matt Fitzpatrick impresses on low-scoring day at Le Golf National English duo Matt Fitzpatrick and Sam Bairstow two behind early leader Michael Kim at Le Golf National; Tommy Fleetwood and Viktor Hovland among the other Ryder Cup stars in action; watch live on Friday from 12.30pm on Sky Sports Golf Thursday 24 September 2026 19:05, UK Image: Matt Fitzpatrick made a bogey-free start to his FedEx Open de France return Matt Fitzpatrick sits two shots off the early lead at the FedEx Open de France, as defending champion Michael Kim topped the leaderboard after a ‘dream start’ at Le Golf National. Kim carded eight birdies, including four of his first six holes, to post a bogey-free 63 on a low-scoring opening day and grab a two-shot advantage. The American - beginning on the back nine - followed successive birdies from the 11th by adding two more from the 14th, then ended a run of pars by picking up a shot at the par-four first. messages.text: Russell outpaces Antonelli to continue flying start in Azerbaijan

metadata.summary: George Russell completed an impressive practice double as he outpaced title-leading team-mate Kimi Antonelli in a dominant start to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend.
metadata.content: Azerbaijan GP: George Russell fastest in second practice ahead of Kimi Antonelli in dominant start in Baku | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Azerbaijan GP: George Russell fastest in second practice ahead of Kimi Antonelli in dominant start in Baku Mercedes make a commanding start to the Azerbaijan weekend, with George Russell in early flying form; Red Bull's Max Verstappen only driver within one second of Mercedes' pace; watch final practice in Baku on Friday at 9.30am, with Qualifying at 1pm, live on Sky Sports F1 Thursday 24 September 2026 15:15, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Thursday's practice sessions at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. George Russell completed an impressive practice double as he outpaced title-leading team-mate Kimi Antonelli in a dominant start to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend. ​​Mercedes' Russell built on the form that had seen him top the day's earlier first practice session to stay at the head of the timesheet, this time finishing with a half-second advantage around the challenging streets of Baku. Antonelli, who leads Russell by 81 points in the chase for 2026's Drivers' Championship, experienced a compromised Thursday owing to the hydraulic leak that stopped his car midway through the opening session.
